Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct)
Second or Greater Recurrent Disc Herniation

Required findings: Individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.

Imaging findings include degenerative spondylolisthesis without spondylolysis with EITHER dynamic segmental instability on flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of a supine and upright image (difference in translational alignment >3mm) OR Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis.

OR imaging findings include spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis (e.g., Isthmic Spondylolisthesis) with ANY of: Meyerding Grade I or II anterolisthesis with plain x-rays supporting progression; Meyerding Grade III or higher anterolisthesis with ≥50% anterior slippage OR plain x-rays supporting progression; progressive spinal pain without confirmatory imaging showing progression; multi-level spondylolysis on plain x-rays; post-operative instability from facet joint excision exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% of a single facet; pars fracture; or previous spinal decompression resulting in iatrogenic spondylolisthesis.

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) within normal range.

Required findings: Individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.

Anticipated iatrogenic instability created by: disruption of posterior elements due to facet joint excision exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% of a single facet; removal of the pars interarticularis requiring fusion; decompression for Meyerding Grade I or higher spondylolisthesis with foraminal stenosis; or complete/partial corpectomy (removal of at least one-third of vertebral body, not for osteophytes alone).

Imaging findings include coronal plane deformity with ANY of: Cobb angle >30°; asymmetric disk collapse causing symptomatic foraminal narrowing; or global coronal imbalance causing head and trunk shift off the midline.
OR imaging findings include sagittal imbalance with ANY of: sagittal vertebral axis measurement >8cm; or pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis >15°.

Required findings: Individual is a candidate for an initial primary lumbar discectomy per CMM-606.2: Initial Primary Lumbar Microdiscectomy or CMM 606.1: General Guidelines.

Advanced imaging shows ANY of: primary extraforaminal disc herniation at L5-S1 where far lateral approach is not feasible due to iliac wings; primary foraminal disc herniation requiring facet resection for retrieval resulting in iatrogenic instability; or primary disc herniation at the level of the spinal cord (low lying conus medullaris).

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) within normal range.

Non-Indications: Lumbar fusion is not medically necessary if the individual is not a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.

For Actual Instability, fusion is not indicated if imaging does not show degenerative spondylolisthesis with specific instability metrics (>3mm translation or Grade II+), or spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis meeting specific grade/progression criteria, unless instability is identified intra-operatively.

For Anticipated Iatrogenic Instability, fusion is not indicated if the instability is not created by specific posterior element disruption (>50% bilateral/75% single facet), pars removal, decompression for Grade I+ spondylolisthesis with foraminal stenosis, or corpectomy (>1/3 vertebral body).

For Adult Symptomatic Degenerative Spinal Deformity, fusion is not indicated if imaging does not show coronal deformity (Cobb >30°, asymmetric collapse, global imbalance) or sagittal imbalance (axis >8cm, PI-LL >15°).

For Initial Disc Herniation, fusion is not indicated unless the herniation is extraforaminal at L5-S1 (infeasible far lateral approach), foraminal requiring facet resection causing instability, or at the level of the spinal cord.
For Recurrent Disc Herniation, fusion is not indicated if there is no evidence of anterolisthesis with dynamic instability (>3mm) or Meyerding Grade II or higher.
Fusion is not medically necessary if the individual has not documented nicotine-free status (never-smoker or 6+ weeks abstinence validated by cotinine testing).
Important criteria & exceptions: Criteria exception for Actual Instability: When instability is created and/or identified intra-operatively, the pre-operative imaging criteria are NOT required.
Nicotine-free status must be validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the specific testing method and lab.
Corpectomy for Anticipated Iatrogenic Instability must involve removal of at least one-third of the vertebral body and is not covered for resection of osteophytes alone.
Documentation required: Objective cotinine testing results (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range, or documentation of never-smoker status.
Dynamic segmental instability imaging: flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of supine and upright images showing >3mm translational alignment difference.
Plain x-rays supporting progression of anterolisthesis (for spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis).
Imaging demonstrating Meyerding Grade (I, II, or III+) spondylolisthesis.
Imaging demonstrating Cobb angle >30°, asymmetric disk collapse, global coronal imbalance, sagittal vertebral axis >8cm, or pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis >15° (for deformity).
Advanced imaging (MRI/CT) showing primary extraforaminal, foraminal, or intradural disc herniation characteristics.
Documentation of facet joint excision percentage (>50% bilateral or 75% single) or pars interarticularis removal.
Documentation of vertebral body removal percentage (≥1/3) for corpectomy.
